question: How does an order get placed and paid?
title: Placing an order
summary: The Place order button checks the cart with a dry-run create, then POSTs the order to the API. The API only stores a `pending` order. A separate polling loop, the order worker, reserves the stock, creates one charge at the payment provider and flips the order to `charging`. The provider sends the customer to their bank; the worker polls the provider every 2 s until the charge succeeded, then marks the order paid. The page polls the order every 3 s.

nodes.label: Web shop (browser)
nodes.summary: Where the customer starts: the checkout page in the browser. Builds the order, sends it, waits for the payment.

nodes.summary: One Go binary holding both the HTTP API and the worker loop that does the actual payment work.

nodes.label: Payment provider
nodes.summary: The card payment company. It holds each charge, sends the customer to their bank when the bank asks for it, and calls the shop's webhook. Third-party code.

nodes.label: Customer's bank
nodes.summary: The bank behind the customer's card. Its 3-D Secure page asks the customer to confirm the payment. Third-party code.

nodes.label: payment settings
nodes.summary: The provider settings the shop ships: when 3-D Secure is asked for, which events come back, when a charge expires.

anchor.text:
# The payment provider, as the shop talks to it. Charges are created by the worker (payments/charge.go);
# the provider then sends the customer to their bank for 3-D Secure and calls the webhook below when it knows.
provider:
  name: examplepay
  apiBase: https://api.examplepay.test/v1
  # auto: 3-D Secure only when the bank asks for it; always: every charge.
  threeDSecure: auto
  webhook:
    path: /api/payments/webhook
    events: [charge.succeeded, charge.failed, charge.expired]
  # A charge the bank has not answered in this time expires on the provider's side.
  chargeTimeout: 15m
  retries: 3

steps.title: The page checks the cart first, then sends the order
The API only writes a pending order
Asynchronous hop 1: the worker polls the database
The order is not sent as is: it becomes the provider's charge
Everything goes into one charge request with the order's key
Create the charge, flip to charging
Asynchronous hop 2: the provider asks the bank (not our code)
Asynchronous hop 3: the bank answers the provider (not our code)
Every 2 s: is it paid? Answered by the provider only
The progress message is inferred, not reported
Asynchronous hop 4: the page (and the order page) poll the order
